First release of `carve-lang`, the Python binding for the
[Carve](https://markup-carve.github.io/carve/) markup language.

The parser is not reimplemented in Python. This is a PyO3 binding over
[carve-rs](https://github.com/markup-carve/carve-rs), so output is
byte-identical to the Rust CLI for the same input.

The distribution is `carve-lang`; the import stays `carve`.

```bash
pip install carve-lang
```

```python
import carve

carve.to_html("# Hello *world*")
```

### Renderers

`to_html`, `to_markdown`, `to_plain_text`, `to_ansi`.

### Options

- `extensions=[...]` enables opt-in extensions by name; `extensions()` lists
  what this build accepts.
- `mode="static"` flattens interactive constructs to self-contained HTML, and
  `renderers={...}` supplies build-time renderers for diagram fences and math. A
  missing or failing renderer degrades to the construct's source, never to
  nothing.
- `symbols={...}` maps `:name:` symbols. Values are inserted as **trusted raw
  output** - never build this map from untrusted input.
- `profile=` (`full`, `article`, `comment`, `minimal`) restricts which
  constructs are allowed and caps input length. A rejection raises, rather than
  returning the engine's empty string, which a caller could not tell from a
  document that legitimately rendered to nothing.
- `safe=True` escapes `=html` raw passthrough. The normative hardening - URL
  scheme denylist, event-handler attributes, Trojan-Source bidi characters - is
  always on and needs no argument.

### AST and provenance

- `parse` / `parse_json` export the PART 12 AST, the interchange shape every
  Carve engine publishes.
- `read_stamp` reads a `carve fmt --stamp` provenance marker; `needs_review`
  answers whether a document predates the spec version this engine targets. An
  unstamped document answers `True`, since unknown provenance is not the same as
  current.

### Wheels

abi3 (`abi3-py38`), so one wheel per platform covers CPython 3.8 and newer, with
`carve.pyi` type stubs.

### Engine

Embeds carve-rs `4ddc24a0`, which renders the full spec corpus byte-identically.
